issues: [assembly] BLOCKER. The per-algorithm generated tree does not exist: generated/leastttftjoint/ holds only leastttftjoint_config.yaml and leastttftjoint_output.json, and all 35 declared files_created paths plus the one files_modified path have no copy there. The focal arm in this same translation carries generated/causalsloexternality/{cmd,pkg}, and the prior v0.9.0 translation of this arm carries .../ef2cd961.../generated/leastttftjoint/{cmd,pkg}, so this is a gap rather than a change of convention. Content exists at snapshots/leastttftjoint/v3/ and all 35 plugin paths were verified byte-identical to the checkout with no undeclared files, so a copy suffices -- except cmd/epp/runner/runner.go, which in v3 still carries the pre-12:43 wording and must come from the checkout.

[assembly] BLOCKER. The focal arm's manifest and generated tree are stale with respect to the seam, and this breaks the baseline toggle. generated/causalsloexternality/causalsloexternality_output.json:files_created lists 27 paths for the shared package and omits arm.go and evalfixture.go, while leastttftjoint_output.json lists 29 for the same package. The focal generated tree differs from the checkout on policy.go, handler.go, picker.go, config.go, README.md, config_test.go, overlay_test.go and policy_test.go (all pre-seam), and arm.go/evalfixture.go are absent. Consequence (a): restore_baseline walks the declared list, so toggling the FOCAL arm to baseline removes its 27 files and leaves arm.go and evalfixture.go behind as untracked source referencing newPolicy, newShadowTable, newPluginMetrics, registerMetrics, Config, Snapshot and sloClassStandard, none of which still exist -- the BASELINE image then fails to compile. Consequence (b): the focal arm has two divergent sources of truth for the same 29 files, so materialising its tree after this one silently reverts the seam and breaks leastttftjoint's build. Fix: add arm.go and evalfixture.go to the focal arm's files_created and re-materialise generated/causalsloexternality/pkg/... from the current checkout so both manifests describe the same 29 files with the same contents.

[code-quality] objective.go:70-73 is factually wrong about the shared producer binding, in the place designated as this arm's canonical documentation. It claims the producers 'are declared once in the BASELINE overlay and inherited, which is what makes that binding shared rather than per-arm'. pluginsCustomConfig's custom-plugins.yaml value is a scalar string, so the treatment overlay's string replaces the baseline's entirely, and this arm's overlay does re-declare both token-producer and approx-prefix-cache-producer itself. Nothing is inherited: the binding is shared because the baseline and both treatment overlays restate identical producer names and parameters, maintained by hand across three files rather than by the merge. Values are identical today, so this is a documentation defect rather than a behavioural one, but a reader who believes it will edit the baseline, assume both arms followed, and never check that the two treatment overlays still agree -- the 'second, differently-configured signal' hazard of config.md section 5 signal 11 arriving through the documentation.

[code-quality] Matching test gap: TestOverlayIsCommonModeWithTheFocalArmOutsideTheObjective compares comparator.Signals != focal.Signals, which covers the producer NAMES but not the producer plugin ENTRIES. Two overlays could bind the same tokenizedPromptProducerName while declaring token-producer with a different vllm.url or modelName, and every current assertion would pass. Extend the test to compare the token-producer and approx-prefix-cache-producer entries (type, name, parameters) across the two overlays.
reviews.summary: Central design decision accepted and independently verified rather than taken on trust: sharing instead of copying is the stronger reading of the verbatim-copy contract, the whole shared package was diffed against the focal arm's approved snapshot and every change is either seam plumbing or behaviour-preserving for the focal arm, capacityLive() is identical to the old !NoCapacity for an objective returning true, the bookCapacityWork guard changes nothing because capacity.go:143 already early-returns, the three focal test edits are mechanical, Cost matches algorithms/least_ttft_joint.go operand for operand, sortedByID runs at policy.go:668-669 before the objective's ordering choice, and the 1e-12 strict-improvement threshold is intact at :726. No changes requested to EvalFixture (verified not a back door: Eval's fields are unexported, Build reaches only unexported constructors, and table.stop is sync.Once-guarded) beyond an optional doc clause noting the fixture never calls startSweeper so a fixture-built table never reaps. No changes requested on D1's direction; the reviewer re-derived the partial derivatives from the code and confirmed the single-sign summary would have been wrong. Also confirmed: the focal README correction is accurate and one paragraph in scope, the router.epp.flags correction is right at this pin, the cross-arm binding guard is a real hazard correctly closed and comparing handler.arm.HandlerType rather than the Arm struct is right since Arm carries an interface field, the overlay is a valid scenario overlay named pdinfocomm3, the parameter block is a strict subset with all seven shared blocks value-identical and exactly the five SLO-value keys absent, both coefficient sets match config.md section 4 to the last digit, and the converse undeclared-file check over the checkout is clean at 35 declared and 35 present.
